findings.title: Issue pages have no links to the sources
findings.fixed_when: each story on an issue page links to its original, as /archive/6/ does. Each Science corner paper links to the paper.
findings.observed: Recent issue pages name a source as plain text ("TechCrunch; also Bloomberg Technology", "arXiv · AI research") and the story titles are not links. External links inside the issue body: /archive/472 0 (20 stories), 473 0 (12), 477 0 (12), 450 0 (20), 462 0 (20), 451 0 (20), 446 0 (12 papers), 169 0 (6). The oldest issue, /archive/6 (29 Sep), still has 80 links for 40 stories, and the Notes essay /archive/471 has 48. Terms: "Every note links to its source, and you should read the source before you rely on a claim." Privacy: "each with a link to the original." For Science corner papers there is no link to the paper anywhere: on the front page the 5 paper titles link to /archive/446/, and that page links nowhere.
findings.expected: Each story on an issue page links to its original, as the front page does and as /archive/6 did, so a reader can follow the Terms advice to read the source.
steps: Open /archive/472/ (the "AI daily, 24-Nov-26 →" link on the front page)
Try to open the source of any story, for example "Sierra raises $1.75B Series F" (TechCrunch). Neither the title nor the source name is a link.
Compare /archive/6/, where every story title is a link
findings.suggested_fix: Render the story title (or the source name) as a link to the primary source URL in the web view of an issue, as in the September template and on the front page. For Science corner, link the arXiv page.

findings.title: A source line and an "author has a stake" note are missing

findings.observed: On / and /ai-in-management/ (EN), "Products / Joanna Stern says Siri AI still fails basics on the HomeView despite Apple's Google partnership" has no source line; the next story follows at once. /ru/ shows "Bloomberg Tech · у автора есть доля: …" and /archive/451 shows "Bloomberg Tech · at 17:08 · author has a stake: Joanna Stern is arguing from her own HomeView review …". The "author has a stake" warning matters most and is the part that is missing.
findings.expected: Every front-page story shows its source line, including the stake label, in EN as in RU.
steps: Open /, scroll to "PODCASTS AND TALKS ABOUT AI, 22-NOV-26"
Compare with the same item on /ru/
findings.suggested_fix: Check the EN teaser template for items with a stake label (the source line seems to be dropped when the label is present or too long).

Same on /ru/about/ ("{labeled} заметок за эту неделю прошли проверку"). Every other step shows a number (5,730 / 11 / 2,648 / 178 / 8,282 / 11). The same page also shows "Explainer video: coming".

findings.title: Story counts are higher than the stories shown
findings.fixed_when: each count equals the stories on its issue page, or the issue page lists the rest.
findings.observed: Archive / group-page count vs stories on the issue page: AI daily 24-Nov (/archive/472) "28 stories" vs 20; AI daily 22-Nov (450) "37 stories" vs 20; India & AI 24-Nov (477) "18 stories" vs 12; Ethiopia daily brief 24-Nov (473) "14 stories" vs 12; AI daily 23-Nov (462) "23 stories" vs 20. Matching: Podcasts 22-Nov (451) 20/20, Ethiopia AI weekly 21-Oct (169) 6/6, 29 Sep (6) 40/40. Several issues show exactly 20 stories, so the page seems to be capped at 20 while the count includes all candidates.
findings.expected: The count next to an issue equals the number of stories a reader finds when they open it.
steps: Open /archive/ and read "AI daily, 22-Nov-26 … 37 stories"
Open it (/archive/450/) and count the stories under the topic headings (20)
findings.suggested_fix: Compute "N stories" from the stories actually rendered in the issue (after the cap or selection), or show the rest under a "more stories" list on the issue page.

findings.title: The Anthropic IPO figures need context
findings.fixed_when: each figure says what it includes ("including the private placement"), and valuation is not called IPO size.
findings.observed: Front page, AI in Management: lead "pricing its shares at $83 … The offering of 980 million shares was the largest IPO on record" (980M × $83 = $81.3B), then "Anthropic raises $107.3 billion in IPO at $83 per share" (implies 1.29B shares), then "Anthropic CFO says company has raised almost $120 billion in IPO". Group page issue leads: 12-Nov "seeks up to $90.4 billion", 16-Nov "Anthropic's $1.4 trillion IPO" (a valuation called an IPO), 22-Nov "Raising About $119.5 Billion Gross" (IPO and private placement). Podcast issue 451: "implied valuation is near $2 trillion"; 8-Nov "targeting $1.5tn valuation". None of these says how the figures relate.
findings.expected: When figures for one event conflict, the summary says which is which (base offering vs greenshoe vs private placement, valuation vs proceeds), or the site uses one reconciled figure. "$1.4 trillion IPO" should read "$1.4 trillion valuation".
steps: Open / and read the three Anthropic items in AI in Management
Open /ai-in-management/ and read the Every issue leads for 12-Nov, 16-Nov, 19-Nov, 22-Nov
findings.suggested_fix: In the credibility or editing step, flag numeric conflicts between notes on the same event and add the qualifier ("including the private placement", "valuation"). Fix the 16-Nov headline wording.

assert_bug_present.text_present: Anthropic raises $107.3 billion in IPO at $83 per share

The same pair is on /subscribe/ ("Mon, Wed" beside "every Tuesday and Thursday"), the front page says "· Mon, Wed", /ru says "пн, ср". The latest issue (/archive/471) is headed "NOTES ON AGENTIC WORK — TUESDAY, 24 NOVEMBER 2026". Older issues in the group are dated Fri 2, 9, 16, 23, 30 Oct, Wed 28 Oct and Tue 10 Nov. The 4 newest have no date in their archive title ("Software Work Needs Evidence Beyond Passing Tests"), unlike every other publication.

Open /subscribe/, read the Notes on Agentic Work row
Open /archive/471/ and read the date line

findings.title: "Dispatches from Others" is offered, but its last issue was 2 November
findings.fixed_when: it shows new issues again, or it is marked paused, or it leaves /subscribe/.
findings.observed: /subscribe/ offers "Interesting Politics · Dispatches from Others … Sun–Fri" with hours 09:00–21:00. /about/: "The Observatory has four desks: AI, Ethiopia, India and Interesting Politics". /archive/ filter "Dispatches from Others": newest issue "Dispatches from Others, 2-Nov-26", 22 days ago, while every other daily publication has an issue on 24-Nov. The front page menu and the topic tabs list only 5 groups, with no Interesting Politics page. The lead "OUR COUNTRY AGAINST THE WORLD" repeats on 10 issues in a row (15–27 Oct). Terms and Privacy describe the service as "about artificial intelligence and Ethiopia" (no India, no politics desk).
findings.expected: Either the publication runs and has a group page like the others, or it is marked paused or ended on /subscribe/ and /about/ (Terms promise to tell subscribers before ending a publication).
steps: Open /subscribe/, find "Dispatches from Others · Sun–Fri"
Open /archive/, click the "Dispatches from Others" filter, read the newest date (2-Nov-26)
findings.suggested_fix: Mark it paused ("paused since 2 Nov") or remove it from /subscribe/ and from the About desk count. If it is active, find out why it stopped sending.

Open /ai-in-management/ and look for AI daily 6-Nov-26

findings.title: An issue page doesn't say which issue it is
findings.fixed_when: each issue starts with its name and date, with previous and next links. That heading would also give these pages the main heading they lack (see the last section).
findings.observed: On 11 of 12 issue pages checked (all but the Notes essay 471), the body starts with "← The archive", then the group link and bullets. The issue name and date ("Ethiopia daily brief, 29-Oct-26") appear only in the browser tab title. The only visible date is the masthead "Tuesday, 24 November 2026", so an old issue reads as today's. There is no previous/next link between issues of a publication, only "← The archive".
findings.expected: A visible heading with publication and date ("Ethiopia daily brief · Thursday, 29 October 2026") at the top of each issue, plus "← previous / next →" within the publication.
steps: Open /archive/264/ (Ethiopia daily brief, 29-Oct-26)
Look for the issue date on the page, then look for a way to the next or previous brief
findings.suggested_fix: Render the issue title as the page h1 (this also fixes the known missing-h1 item) and add prev/next links by publication.

findings.title: Old leads come back, and Science corner entries look the same
findings.fixed_when: a repeat lead is marked ("first reported 2 Nov") or skipped, and each Science corner entry shows its top paper.
findings.observed: "Awash Bank applies for Djibouti banking licence, weighs Awash Group entity" leads Ethiopia daily brief 2-Nov and Ethiopian banking and fintech 13-Nov (11 days later). "National Bank of Ethiopia issues Directive No. FS/01/2026 launching a regulatory sandbox" leads the daily brief 18-Nov and banking 20-Nov. "Anthropic Files for IPO on Nasdaq Under Ticker ANT" leads both AI daily and Podcasts on 28-Oct, and "Google DeepMind's Keerthana Gopalakrishnan on Gemini Robotics 2" leads both on 4-Oct. On /ai-science-corner/ and /archive/, all 8 Science corner issues read "Research papers of the week on AI and the fields around it, in plain English: …" with no lead or count, so a reader cannot tell them apart.
findings.expected: A weekly digest leads with the week's new story, or marks a repeat ("first reported 2 Nov"). Science corner entries show their top paper and a count like the other publications.
steps: Open /ethiopia/, find "Awash Bank applies for Djibouti" twice in "Every issue"
Open /ai-science-corner/ and read the 8 issue entries
findings.suggested_fix: Exclude notes already used as the lead of another issue in the last N days from lead selection, or label them as follow-ups. Use the top paper title as the Science corner archive lead.

findings.title: The Ethiopia AI weekly is short and repeats itself
findings.fixed_when: one event appears once per issue, leads match the desk's topic, and counts read "1 story".
findings.observed: Issue counts: 18-Nov "3 stories", 11-Nov "1 stories", 4-Nov "2 stories". /archive/169 (21-Oct, 6 stories): "Ethiopia Seeks Partner Support for AI Institutions at Bangkok Roundtable" (Fana, "Tigist Fisseha") and "Ethiopia Joins AI Roundtable at IMF and World Bank Meetings" (Ministry of Finance, "Tiguist Fisseha") are the same event with the name spelled two ways. "Ethiopia Ties AI and Digital Skills to Jobs Agenda" (Fana) and "Ethiopia Pursues Private Financing for AI…" (Birr Metrics) are the same speech. "ThatsApp — OpenGradient Announces Decentralized AI Model Hub With Bittensor and Nvidia" (Telebirr Telegram) is not about Ethiopia, yet it is the lead shown for this issue in /archive/ and on /ethiopia/. About promises: "Accounts of the same event are compared and the best is chosen". Also "1 stories" grammar (2 places), and a "Ethiopia daily brief, 29-Oct-26" with 1 story (a company statement).
findings.expected: One story per event, on-topic items only, and an issue skipped (or merged) when there are fewer than 3 stories.
steps: Open /ethiopia/ and read the "Every issue" counts for Ethiopia AI weekly
Open /archive/169/ and compare the Fana and Ministry of Finance stories, and the Fana and Birr Metrics stories
findings.suggested_fix: Run the same-event merge across sources inside weekly issues; apply the desk scope rule to Telegram items (OpenGradient); set a minimum story count for a weekly issue; use plural rules ("1 story").

Open /ru/ and look at the Agentic Software Engineering section
